clue.text: Recommend, say, cat fur

parts.note: to recommend something is to tip it, as with a racing tip
a cat, say, is an example of a domestic pet

explanation.surface: Someone advising on a feline fur garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the cat as one example of the wider word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a fur cape or stole worn round the shoulders.

clue.text: In France, you rise as teacher appears

parts.note: the French familiar word for you is tu
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A French scene where everyone stands as the teacher enters.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common in place names in the west of England such as Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or instructor.

clue.text: Magazine policy to be the last word in humour?

parts.note: Punch was a long-running British humorous magazine
a party line is a policy

explanation.surface: Asks whether a magazine's editorial policy should be the ultimate in comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNCH was a famous British satirical weekly; the definition is playful, the closing words of a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The final line of a joke delivers the laugh, literally the closing words of the humour.

clue.text: Changing at junction

explanation.surface: Something altering at a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning means altering or becoming different; a turning is also a side road branching off at a junction.

clue.text: It's nonsense to applaud, having rejected part

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

indicators.note: rejected signals turning the word part back the other way

explanation.surface: Claims it is silly to cheer after having turned down a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns PART back to TRAP, which follows CLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: Agree Cardiff has representation from diplomat

indicators.note: a representation is a new rendering, so these letters are recast

explanation.surface: Diplomatic consent from Cardiff, the Welsh capital, voiced by an envoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges AGREE CARDIFF HAS, fifteen letters, into the diplomatic title; Cardiff is the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge d'affaires is a diplomat deputising for an ambassador or heading a minor mission.

clue.text: Drug users' sums one court impounded

definitions.note: the clue's possessive is read as a plain plural, the apostrophe being surface only

indicators.note: impounded means locked up, so the second pieces are held inside

parts.note: to sum is to add, so sums gives adds
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Addicts' arithmetic, with one court seizing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impounded' places I and CT inside ADDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Addicts are people dependent on narcotics.

clue.text: Curl right round fireplace

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: RT is the abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A curl of hair lying round the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts RT around INGLE; Rt is the short form of right in the title Rt Hon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long curl of hair.

clue.text: Inclined earlier to be phoney?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
inclined means tended, as in tended to

explanation.surface: Wonders if leaning a certain way beforehand makes someone a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: PRE comes earlier, in front of TENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretended as an adjective means feigned or sham.

clue.text: One making application to hide old coin

explanation.surface: A worker applying something to conceal a vintage coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' is an animal skin, not concealment. A TANNER was the old British sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanner treats animal skins with tannin; a tanner was also slang for the pre-decimal British sixpence.

clue.text: Interview concert-goers

explanation.surface: A talk with people attending a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal interview, as with the Pope; it is also the assembled listeners at a performance.

clue.text: Correcting essay that's read out

indicators.note: read out signals a word as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: an essay is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Marking an essay that is being recited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' gives a word that sounds like WRITING.
explanation.definitionFit: Righting a wrong means putting it straight.

clue.text: Dog is mine but last two letters went missing

indicators.note: the clue says the closing pair of the synonym for mine has gone

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A dog said to be mine, but with some letters lost.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLIERY, a coal mine, drops its final RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a Scottish sheepdog breed.

clue.text: Get rebuked as judge comes into court

explanation.surface: Someone told off as the judge enters the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'be wigged': to wig someone is an old word for scolding them. British judges wear wigs in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To wig is to scold, so to be scolded is to be wigged; wearing a wig describes a British judge in court.

clue.text: Cheap wedding ring for musicians?

parts.note: brass is a cheap alloy compared with gold
a wedding ring is a band

explanation.surface: A cheap wedding ring for a group of players.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'ring' is really a band of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band is a group of players of trumpets, cornets, tubas and the like.

clue.text: Girl meets boy, with added piquancy

parts.note: Sal is a short girl's name
Ted is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A romance spiced up when a girl meets a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Salted food has extra savour from added salt, as in a tale spiced up.

clue.text: Be quick making appearance with instrument

parts.note: looks are a person's appearance
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Hurrying to perform with an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Look sharp is an idiom urging someone to hurry up.

clue.text: A sinful desire of one mind

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Everyone united in one wicked craving.
explanation.definitionFit: People who agree are in accord, sharing the same view.

clue.text: Improves appearance of vicar with current measures

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a vicar's title
amps measure electrical current

explanation.surface: A vicar's new methods to smarten things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is electrical current, not present-day.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or give a fresh look.

clue.text: Infection may make you die full of salt water

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: taken as written
seas are bodies of salt water

explanation.surface: Warns that illness might kill you after swallowing seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts SEAS inside DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is an illness, often caused by infection.

clue.text: Still under blanket?

parts.note: suggests someone lying abed, but describes being unable to move because of a thick blanket of mist

explanation.surface: Someone still in bed under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fogbound means stuck in place by fog, which is often called a blanket.

clue.text: Badly bit legs and other organs

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone badly bitten on the legs and elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges BIT LEGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Giblets are edible internal organs of poultry, such as liver and heart.

clue.text: A rugby competition, even on board ship

indicators.note: on board means contained within the vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby game played even aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts EVEN inside SS, steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is rugby union played with seven a side, often in tournaments.

clue.text: A call for help to install finest fire-proof material

indicators.note: install means put in, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
best means finest

explanation.surface: Someone calling out for help to fit premium fireproofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to install' puts BEST inside SOS, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral used for heat-resistant insulation.

clue.text: Miserably underhand about notice

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: sly means underhand or crafty
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: An unhappy, devious response to a notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SLY around AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadly means in an unhappy manner.

clue.text: Clumsily cram cheap upholstery material-into this?

definitions.text: Clumsily cram cheap upholstery material-into this?

indicators.note: clumsily means done awkwardly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: horsehair was a cheap stuffing for furniture

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly stuffing cheap padding into a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsily' rearranges CRAM to ARMC, then HAIR follows; the whole clue describes upholstering the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded chair with side rests is stuffed with such material.

clue.text: Times editor removed

parts.note: eras are times or periods

explanation.surface: The Times editor has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Erased means wiped out or deleted.

clue.text: Harass girl with pressure

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
stress is pressure

explanation.surface: Pressuring a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress is to upset or trouble someone.

clue.text: Provide in flexible fashion!

explanation.surface: Supply delivered supplely.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply means furnish; supply as an adverb also means in a supple, pliant way.
